canon: GNHL team ids in gnhl_parent come from world-assets/lore/canon.json teams[].id. bri (Bramford Iron) and rsr (Redstone Rockets) have no CHA affiliate.
note: RinkGM club and league canon. Clubs are listed in league order: per tier, the first N non-expansion clubs fill LeagueTiers.TIERS[tier].teams.

leagues.name: Valley Beer League, D Division
leagues.trophy_desc: A dented pewter beer stein bolted to a hockey puck. The engraving plate ran out in 2011, so winners now write their names on masking tape.
leagues.division_note: Named for the 9:30 pm and 11:15 pm ice slots. Purely for the standings page.

leagues.name: Valley Beer League, C Division
leagues.trophy_desc: A two-litre glass mug etched with a moose. Filled once by the winners, emptied quickly, returned sticky.
leagues.division_note: Named for the nights the teams usually play.

leagues.name: Valley Beer League, A Division
leagues.trophy_desc: Officially the Frostbank Valley Championship. Everyone calls it the Gord, after the bronze bust of Big Gord Halvorsen he donated in 1998 without being asked.
leagues.division_note: Named for the two sheets at Harlow Falls Municipal.

leagues.name: Northern Senior Hockey Association
leagues.trophy_desc: A real silver cup from 1922, donated by Kessler mill owner Thaddeus Aldous. It has been dropped through the ice of Port Ainsley lake once (1962) and recovered by a man in waders.
leagues.division_note: Valley-road towns against the lakeside and up-the-pass towns.

leagues.name: Interlake Hockey League
leagues.official: Interlake Hockey League, presented by Rink Rage
leagues.trophy_desc: The original 1979 trophy was a chrome jerry can on a walnut base, because the founder ran a gas station. The new one is nicer. Nobody calls it anything but the Gas Can.
leagues.division_note: Lake and port towns against the inland rail and mining cities.

leagues.name: Continental Hockey Association
leagues.official: Continental Hockey Association, official development league of the GNHL
leagues.trophy_desc: A heavy oak shield with a silver maple leaf for every champion since 1951. Two trainers carry it; it does not get skated around.
leagues.division_note: Northern and forestry cities against the steel and port cities.

swarm.desc: Everyone chases the puck. Beer league classic.

run_and_gun.desc: Fly the zone, trade chances, forget defence.

physical.desc: Finish every check, lift every stick.

trap.desc: Clog the neutral zone, sit on leads.

possession.desc: Keep the puck, make the extra pass, wait for a lane.

dump_and_chase.desc: Chip it deep, go get it, grind the corners.

shoot_everything.desc: Any angle, any distance, right now.

goalie_dependent.desc: A great goalie behind a so-so team.

clubs.name: Wobbly Pops
clubs.sponsor: The Wobbly Pop Tap & Grill, Millbrook Main Street
clubs.identity: Dads who learned to skate the same winter their kids did, and refuse to be outdone by a nine-year-old.

notable.name: Gary Pruett
notable.note: Learned to stop last February and now does it at every opportunity, preferably in front of the bench.

clubs.name: Millbrook Molars
clubs.sponsor: Haverkamp Family Dentistry
clubs.identity: Four dentists, a hygienist and two patients who could not say no. They hand out toothbrushes in the handshake line.

notable.name: Dr. Lyle Haverkamp
notable.note: Lectures everyone about mouthguards and has never once worn one.

clubs.style_note: They pass constantly because nobody wants to get hit in the hands.

clubs.name: Moose Knuckles
clubs.sponsor: Millbrook Legion Hall, Branch 112
clubs.identity: The 1994 Millbrook Midget AA team, back together for one more run. They were very good in 1994.

notable.name: Rick 'Sauce' Saucier
notable.note: Scored 61 goals in 1994 and has told 61 stories about it since. Gassed by the second period.

clubs.name: Ice Holes
clubs.sponsor: Hat Trick Tavern
clubs.identity: They play for the postgame. The pitcher is pre-ordered for 10:45 and the hockey is in the way.

notable.name: Dwayne Kuzyk
notable.note: Has never missed a postgame and has missed eleven games.

clubs.style_note: Every shot is one step closer to the bar.

clubs.name: Pallbearers
clubs.sponsor: Gilchrist & Sons Funeral Home ("We'll be the last to let you down")
clubs.identity: Quiet, punctual, unfailingly polite. They arrive in the second hearse.

notable.name: Morley Gilchrist III
notable.note: The steadiest hands in the valley, which he says comes with the job. Nobody asks which part.

clubs.name: Flood Crew
clubs.sponsor: Millbrook Parks & Recreation (owner of the rink)
clubs.identity: The rink staff, on their own ice after hours. They know every soft spot and every dead board.

notable.name: Earl Bratt
notable.note: Drives Doris, the 1974 Zambelli, and will not hear a word against her. Uses the Millbrook bank, the dead spot behind the net that Ronnie Haverstock made famous, better than anyone alive except Ronnie.

clubs.name: Frozen Assets
clubs.sponsor: Frostbank, Millbrook branch ("Banking With a Cool Head")
clubs.identity: Tellers, a loans officer and the branch manager. They protect a one-goal lead like an overdraft.

notable.name: Colin Nolan
notable.note: Changes lines with a laminated spreadsheet and charges a late fee for missed shifts.

clubs.name: Sin Bin Brewers
clubs.sponsor: Sin Bin Brewpub, Harlow Falls
clubs.identity: Craft beer people. Every beer on the tap list is named after a penalty, and they have earned all of them.

notable.name: Cody Lindqvist
notable.note: Leads the division in penalty minutes, almost all of them for explaining the rulebook to referees.

clubs.name: Big Gord's Haulers
clubs.sponsor: Big Gord's Trucks ("Big Gord Won't Let You Walk")
clubs.identity: Big Gord owns the team, picks the lines and plays defence. The roster is whoever is on the lot that week.

notable.name: Gordon 'Big Gord' Halvorsen
notable.note: Has sold trucks from the same lot outside Kessler since 1977 and stars in every advert, shouting from a truck bed. Insists on being on the ice for every power play, and shouts from there too.

clubs.name: Plungers
clubs.sponsor: Duffy Bros. Plumbing & Heating ("Number one in the number two business")
clubs.identity: Hot-and-cold split jerseys, like the taps. The best-organised team in C, until someone gets an emergency call mid-game.

notable.name: Terry Duffy
notable.note: Still carries a pager. It goes off about once a game, usually on a breakaway.

clubs.style_note: They know a thing or two about clogs.

clubs.name: Millbrook Mallards
clubs.sponsor: Millbrook Dairy (Ronnie Haverstock's old employer)
clubs.identity: The most famous beer league team in hockey. During the 2005 lockout they wrote to the Puckworth Cup trustees asking to be considered, and the Cup came to Millbrook for a night. The photo hangs in the lobby; the players have aged, the handwriting has not.

notable.name: Larry Piche
notable.note: Wrote the 2005 letter in his neat handwriting and has sent the trustees a polite follow-up every March since. Has never received a reply and considers this encouraging.

clubs.style_note: Twenty years together. They know where everyone will be, which helps, because nobody can get there quickly.

clubs.name: Cold Ones
clubs.sponsor: Moosebrew Lager
clubs.identity: Twentysomethings who are sure they are one call away from Senior. They warm up with music on a speaker.

notable.name: Tyler Brandt
notable.note: Played half a season of Junior B in 2017 and brings it up in every handshake line.

clubs.style_note: Every rush ends with a slapshot from the blue line, because Tyler saw it on TV.

clubs.name: Brokenbone Adjusters
clubs.sponsor: Brokenbone Mutual Insurance ("We've Seen Your Slapshot")
clubs.identity: Insurance adjusters who know exactly what every injury costs and play accordingly. They file incident reports on hits.

notable.name: Doug Peterson
notable.note: Has denied two of his own teammates' claims, citing pre-existing conditions (being in the beer league).

clubs.style_note: Risk-averse. Never makes a pass that is not fully covered.

clubs.name: Night Owls
clubs.sponsor: Double-Double Donuts, Harlow Falls (open 24 hours)
clubs.identity: Overnight bakers, two night nurses and a hospital porter. At 11:15 pm they are wide awake and everyone else is not.

notable.name: Shauna Reid
notable.note: The fastest skater in the division. Plays every shift like it is a code blue and brings day-old crullers for the refs.

clubs.name: Maple Tire Retreads
clubs.sponsor: Maple Tire & Muffler, Port Ainsley branch ("We Fix What Winter Breaks")
clubs.identity: Nobody under 45. Every knee has been rebuilt at least once, and the goalie is the reason they still win.

notable.name: Wally Dumont
notable.note: Played two games of Senior for Kessler in 1989. Has stopped everything since and still has the Kessler socks.

clubs.name: Slapshot Saloon
clubs.sponsor: Slapshot Saloon, Harlow Falls
clubs.identity: The best bar team in the valley. They recruit ex-college players with the promise of free wings for life.

notable.name: Brett Kowalski
notable.note: Played four years of small-college hockey and mentions it before, during and after every game.

clubs.name: Hydro Linemen
clubs.sponsor: Harlow Falls Hydro, Local 6 social committee
clubs.identity: Power linemen who climb poles in January blizzards. A bodycheck is a nice break for them.

notable.name: Dale 'Transformer' Hughes
notable.note: Six foot five, kind to animals, has knocked two opponents through the old Pad 2 gate.

clubs.name: Rink Rage Bombers
clubs.sponsor: Rink Rage energy drink ("Taste the Penalty")
clubs.identity: The sponsorship is a cooler of a drink nobody over thirty should touch. They are very, very fast for exactly forty minutes.

notable.name: Jordan 'Jolt' Pelletier
notable.note: Has had a can between every period since 2021. Has not, as far as anyone knows, slept.

clubs.name: Splinter Group
clubs.sponsor: Lou's Second Pint, directly across the street from the Slapshot Saloon
clubs.identity: Formed when half the Slapshot Saloon roster quit over who paid for a pitcher. They have been angry for eight years.

notable.name: Mike Barrett
notable.note: Is still owed $14.50 and keeps the receipt in his helmet.

clubs.name: Backcrackers
clubs.sponsor: Kerr Family Chiropractic
clubs.identity: Run by a chiropractor whose business plan is to fix opponents' backs after the game, for a fee.

notable.name: Dr. Shane Kerr
notable.note: Adjusts his own neck on the bench between shifts. The sound carries.

clubs.name: Smoke Eaters
clubs.sponsor: Kessler Volunteer Fire Department; jersey sponsor Hearthstone Furnaces ("Warm Homes. Cold Ice.")
clubs.identity: Volunteer firefighters. Famous for the postgame chili, and for leaving mid-period when the pagers go off.

notable.name: Captain Doug Ellis
notable.note: Once took a faceoff in full turnout gear after a call. Won it.

clubs.name: Walleyes
clubs.sponsor: Lakeside Bait & Tackle, Port Ainsley
clubs.identity: Ice fishermen and lake guides. The bus smells of minnows and the goalie is unbeatable on a good day.

notable.name: Anton Ruutu
notable.note: Came from Finland for one exchange semester in 2009 and never left. Says the valley reminds him of home, but with worse coffee.

clubs.name: Rusty Blades
clubs.sponsor: The Rusty Blade Pub, Harlow Falls
clubs.identity: The dynasty. Five straight A Division titles, a roster of ex-junior players and a trophy case in the pub's washroom hallway.

notable.name: Dale Fraser
notable.note: Still wears his 1992 Junior C ring under his glove. Treats the A Division like the Olympics.

clubs.name: Kessler Millmen
clubs.sponsor: Community-owned; jersey sponsor Kessler Pulp & Paper
clubs.identity: The oldest club in the north and the loudest building. Eleven Aldous Cups, wooden trusses, standing room, and the smell of the mill when the wind is wrong.

notable.name: Hap Doyle
notable.note: Seventy-one years old. Has been photographed smiling once, in 1996, and denies it.

clubs.name: Millbrook Lumber Kings
clubs.sponsor: Volunteer board; jersey sponsor Grizzly Gas & Go
clubs.identity: Your home town's senior club, in buffalo-plaid jerseys. Last Aldous Cup in 1979. Crowds rise and fall with the state of the Community Arena.

notable.name: Old Pete Vachon
notable.note: Has sharpened every Lumber King's skates since 1971 and keeps the 1979 Cup photo in the skate sharpener's drawer.

clubs.lore_hook: When the user renovates Millbrook Community Arena, the Lumber Kings' attendance and morale can rise with it.

clubs.name: Harlow Falls Huskies
clubs.sponsor: Frostbank
clubs.identity: Tidy, well-run and slightly smug. The best minor hockey system in the valley feeds them, and they will tell you so in their newsletter.

notable.name: Brendan Quinn
notable.note: Wears a tie behind the bench. Has a five-year plan, laminated.

clubs.name: Port Ainsley Lakers
clubs.sponsor: Port Ainsley Marina & Boat Storage
clubs.identity: Fishing-town club. Every February they play one home game outdoors on the frozen lake, and the fans throw a frozen pike after the first goal.

notable.name: Big Nils Olsen
notable.note: Six foot six ice fisherman. Hauls his own ice hut to the Pond Classic and sells coffee out of it at intermission.

clubs.name: Duncannon Foundry
clubs.sponsor: Duncannon Iron Works retirees' association
clubs.identity: The city's original team, in the 1949 downtown Gardens the council keeps trying to demolish. The pro Dukes shared the building until 2009, then left for the Frostbank Centre, and the Foundry have not forgiven them.

notable.name: Marc Leclerc
notable.note: Has filibustered the Gardens demolition vote three times. Plays the same way.

clubs.name: Tollbridge Coal Kings
clubs.sponsor: Tollbridge Rail & Coal
clubs.identity: A rail junction town past the east end of the valley. The Coliseum seats 1,100 and they have sold it out for every playoff game since 1971.

notable.name: Wade 'The Toll' Tkachuk
notable.note: Collects the toll from anyone who crosses the crease. Works as a crossing guard on weekdays and is lovely with children.

clubs.name: Sainte-Odile Castors
clubs.sponsor: Caisse populaire de Sainte-Odile
clubs.identity: A French-speaking lake village with the most skilled team in Senior. They pass the puck like it belongs to them and sing on the bench.

notable.name: Father Marc Gagnon
notable.note: Blesses the sticks before every game. Has received three bench minors for language, which he says were in Latin.

clubs.name: Carver's Gap Ravens
clubs.sponsor: Gap Pass Ski Hill
clubs.identity: Up the mountain pass, two hours by bus when the road is open. The rink is a Quonset hut and visiting teams swear the air is thinner.

notable.name: Petr Novak
notable.note: Came for a ski instructor job in 2004. Still the best goalie in Senior, and the only reason the Ravens make the playoffs.

clubs.name: Port Ainsley Sturgeon
clubs.sponsor: Owned by Marlene Fisk, Fisk Marine & Outboard
clubs.mascot: Sturgie, a seven-foot fish with unsettling eyes
clubs.identity: The lake's own pro-ish team, sharing the Lakeside Arena with the senior Lakers and playing a careful, grinding game in front of 2,200 people in toques. Their 1983 goalie delivered pizzas between games and founded Puckhead Pizza.

notable.name: Coach Dmitri Volkov
notable.note: Former minor pro defenceman who settled here for the fishing. Preaches structure in a voice that never goes above a murmur.

clubs.name: Carrick Junction Rail Barons
clubs.sponsor: Founding member; owned by the Carrick Junction Railway Heritage Society
clubs.mascot: Conductor Cal, who blows a train whistle after every goal and most icings
clubs.identity: A railway city that founded the league. Their rink is a converted locomotive shed, and the goal horn is an actual train horn.

notable.name: Kyle Sullivan
notable.note: Drives a freight train four days a week. Has never been late to a game, which he credits to timetables.

clubs.name: Ellery Smelters
clubs.sponsor: Ellery Nickel Refinery
clubs.mascot: Slag, a soot-covered furnace worker in a hard hat
clubs.identity: A mining and smelting city that likes its hockey the way it likes its work: hot, heavy and loud. The Pit is the most hostile building in the league.

notable.name: Derek 'Anvil' Morrow
notable.note: Leads the league in hits and has never apologised for one. Runs a very popular knitting circle in the off-season.

clubs.name: Cold Harbour Stingrays
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the Cold Harbour Aquarium
clubs.mascot: Ray Charge, a stingray in a lifeguard whistle
clubs.identity: A port city named by people who were honest about the weather, with a team named after a warm-water fish by a marketing committee.

notable.name: Felix Dubois
notable.note: League scoring leader two years running. Signs autographs at the aquarium's touch tank on Sundays.

clubs.name: Wexford Ice Dogs
clubs.sponsor: Owned by Kibble King Pet Foods
clubs.mascot: Biscuit, a husky in a goalie mask
clubs.identity: Owned by a dog-food company, so every promotion night is a dog night. Dogs welcome in section 104. Section 104 is never quiet.

notable.name: Riley Campbell
notable.note: Shoots from anywhere because the owner pays a bonus per shot on goal. The owner has not reconsidered.

clubs.name: Wendover Scholars
clubs.sponsor: Operated with Wendover College
clubs.mascot: Professor Puck, an owl in a mortarboard
clubs.identity: A college town team stocked with grad students and former varsity players. Smart, patient and slightly insufferable.

notable.name: Evan Lindqvist
notable.note: Writing a thesis on the physics of the wrist shot. Corrects the play-by-play announcer on his own time.

clubs.name: Fort Kinnear Timberwolves
clubs.sponsor: Kinnear Forest Products
clubs.mascot: Lobo, a grey wolf with a lumberjack's axe (foam)
clubs.identity: Forestry town at the end of the rail line. The skaters are honest and slow; the goalie is a local legend.

notable.name: Jean-Paul 'Le Mur' Roy
notable.note: Turned down two minor pro contracts to stay near his trapline. The Kennel chants 'MUR' after every save.

clubs.name: Snowden Blizzard
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the City of Snowden tourism board
clubs.mascot: Flurry, a snowman with a hockey stick for an arm
clubs.identity: The snowiest city in the north, according to a sign at the city limit. Their arena is a dome that leaks snowmelt onto the visitors' bench.

notable.name: Sasha Ivanov
notable.note: Fastest skater in the league. Once beat the team bus home on cross-country skis.

clubs.name: Galloway Outlaws
clubs.sponsor: Owned by 'Honest' Abe Larsen, Honest Abe's Auto Plaza
clubs.mascot: Sheriff Deals, a cowboy with a foam megaphone
clubs.identity: Owned by a used-car dealer who appears on the video board between every period. They play like they have something to sell.

notable.name: Honest Abe Larsen
notable.note: Has traded players for cars, twice. One of the cars was better.

clubs.name: Duncannon Dukes
clubs.sponsor: Owned by Frostbank Sports & Entertainment
clubs.mascot: His Grace, a moose in a velvet cape and a small crown (the big crown is Kingsport's)
clubs.identity: The valley's top club and the Kingsport Monarchs' affiliate: one step below monarchs, which is where Kingsport thinks everyone belongs. 5,000 seats since the 2009 move out of the old Gardens, a TeleNorth video board, and a 50/50 draw that once paid for a house. Every renovation you plan is measured against this building.

notable.name: Lorne Pettigrew
notable.note: Keeper of the red rotary phone on his desk, which rings only when Kingsport wants a player. Nobody else in Duncannon is allowed to touch it. Barry 'Suitcase' Pomeroy's seven stints here are on the wall behind it.

clubs.name: Halverton Northmen
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the Halverton Sports Commission
clubs.mascot: Big Olaf, a bearded giant with a foam axe
clubs.identity: A founding member with seven Callahan Shields and a building full of banners. They expect to win and get grumpy when they do not.

notable.name: Coach Bruce Walsh
notable.note: Coached in the GNHL for eleven games in 2014. It ended badly. He would like to go back.

clubs.name: Ravensport Breakers
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the Ravensport Port Authority
clubs.mascot: Bosun, a seagull in a sou'wester
clubs.identity: A big port city that comes alive for hockey. The waterfront arena shakes when the ships blow their horns.

notable.name: Connor Murphy
notable.note: Twenty-year-old prospect with the hardest shot in the league. The GNHL scouts sit in row F.

clubs.name: Marchmont Voyageurs
clubs.sponsor: Owned by a fan co-operative of 4,000 shareholders
clubs.mascot: Pierre le Pagayeur, a voyageur with a canoe paddle
clubs.identity: The fan-owned club. Shareholder meetings are louder than the games, and the games are very loud.

notable.name: Nick Savard
notable.note: Elected captain by 4,000 shareholders after a campaign that included lawn signs.

clubs.name: Tamarack Kodiaks
clubs.sponsor: Owned by Tamarack Credit Union
clubs.mascot: Cubby, a bear who has been in the same suit since 1983
clubs.identity: A northern forestry city that builds big, heavy, slow-to-anger teams, like their parent club in Northgate. Kodiak, the skate maker, has sent a cease-and-desist letter every year since 1983; the club replies with season tickets.

notable.name: Josh Kerr
notable.note: Six foot four, a lumber grader by trade. Reads to schoolchildren every Tuesday and fights someone every Saturday.

clubs.name: Ashcombe Elk
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the Ashcombe Hunting & Angling Club
clubs.mascot: Bugle, an elk whose antlers do not fit through the tunnel
clubs.identity: A quiet, rich town that plays a quiet, careful game. Their goalie steals games they have no business winning.

notable.name: Mats Holmstrom
notable.note: Thirty-four, Swedish, studies opposing shooters on a tablet between periods. Says very little and stops a lot.

clubs.name: Fenwick Firebirds
clubs.sponsor: Owned by Rink Rage Beverage Co. since 2011
clubs.mascot: Phoenix Phil, who is set on (fake) fire during introductions
clubs.identity: The energy drink's flagship team. Pyrotechnics, a DJ, and a playing style best described as caffeinated.

notable.name: Jake Brodeur
notable.note: Has the league's best hands and worst haircut, both paid for by the sponsor.

clubs.name: St. Brendan Friars
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the St. Brendan Abbey Brewery
clubs.mascot: Brother Puck, a monk in a helmet
clubs.identity: Born from a monastery's brewery team. The arena is called the Abbey, the organ plays hymns at faceoffs, and the system is pure discipline. The monks also pray, nightly, for their cursed parent club in Lake Ostrander.

notable.name: Brother Anselm
notable.note: Runs the penalty kill. Has taken a vow of silence that he breaks only to yell at linesmen.

clubs.name: Belle Rive Riptide
clubs.sponsor: Owned by the Belle Rive Waterpark Group
clubs.identity: A 1996 expansion team, signed up three years after its desert parent club in Sunvale, that has never changed its teal-and-purple jerseys, and never will. Their arena has a lazy river behind section 12.

notable.name: Ilya Petrov
notable.note: Former GNHL first-round pick on his third comeback. Absurdly talented on the nights he is interested.

clubs.name: Puckheads
clubs.sponsor: Puckhead Pizza, Millbrook ("Delivered in Under Two Periods")
clubs.identity: Brand new: the delivery drivers from the Millbrook Puckhead, who signed up on a dare. Half of them borrowed their skates.

notable.name: Gino Russo Jr.
notable.note: Plays in a mask painted like a pepperoni puck. Has delivered to the rink between periods, which the league has asked him to stop.

clubs.name: Kessler Overdues
clubs.sponsor: Friends of the Kessler Public Library
clubs.identity: Librarians. Polite off the ice and the dirtiest team in the valley on it. Shhh.

notable.name: Marion Fischer
notable.note: Has never issued a fine she did not collect, on or off the ice.

rivalries.name: The Mill and the Lake
rivalries.story: The oldest feud in the north. In the 1962 final at the Pond Classic a Kessler defenceman fell through soft ice by the boards, the Aldous Cup went in after him, and Port Ainsley won the replay. Kessler says the Lakers cut the ice. Port Ainsley fans have thrown a frozen pike onto the ice after the first goal of every meeting since, and Kessler fans throw back a roll of paper towel.

rivalries.name: The $14.50 Feud
rivalries.story: Two bars across the street from each other. Half the Saloon's roster walked out over an unpaid pitcher and founded the Splinter Group at Lou's Second Pint. The $14.50 has never been repaid; the receipt is in Mike Barrett's helmet. Both bars run a drink special on game night named after the other team's captain.

rivalries.name: The Gardens Grudge
rivalries.story: When the Frostbank Centre opened, the Dukes walked out of the Memorial Gardens they had shared with the Foundry since 1972, and took the Saturday nights, half the crowd and the city's attention with them. The Foundry were left alone in a half-empty 1949 barn the council keeps trying to knock down. They never play each other, so the rivalry runs through council meetings, letters to the Duncannon Daily Ledger and a charity alumni game every March that the Foundry treats as a cup final.

rivalries.name: The Valley Cup
rivalries.story: A September preseason exhibition between the two biggest clubs in the valley. The Dukes treat it as a practice. The Sturgeon treat it as their Puckworth Cup final, and have won it three times, which the Port Ainsley paper has never stopped printing.

rivalries.name: The Billboard War
rivalries.story: Big Gord's Trucks and Maple Tire & Muffler have fought over the same valley billboards for thirty years. The bosses settle it on the ice twice a season, and the loser has to run the winner's ad on their own sign for a month.

rivalries.name: The Toothbrush Incident
rivalries.story: In the Moose Knuckles' first comeback game, Rick Saucier lost a front tooth to a Molars stick. Dr. Haverkamp fixed it the next morning and sent the bill. Saucier has not paid it, the Molars bring it to every game, and the Moose Knuckles now refuse the toothbrushes in the handshake line.

newspapers.name: The Millbrook Clarion
newspapers.note: Weekly, eight pages, beer league scores printed next to the church bake sale.

newspapers.name: The Harlow Falls Herald
newspapers.note: Twice weekly. Very proud of its A Division standings box.

newspapers.name: The Kessler Courier
newspapers.note: Has covered the Millmen since 1921 and has never once been neutral.

newspapers.name: The Port Ainsley Lakesider
newspapers.note: Fishing reports, ice thickness, and the Sturgeon.

newspapers.name: The Duncannon Daily Ledger
newspapers.note: The valley's only daily, with a real sports section and a columnist who hates everything.

radio.name: CKVL 1340 Valley Radio
radio.note: Carries Lumber Kings and Millmen games. Play-by-play by Bernie Szabo, who has called every Kessler home game since 1985 and still pronounces it three different ways.

ladder.scout: Nobody. The C Division captain who saw you at late ice asks if you are free Thursdays.
ladder.travel: Your own car. The heater works if you hit the dash.
ladder.headline: Clarion, page 7: 'Local Skater Moves Up to C; Mother Says She Always Knew'

ladder.scout: The Rusty Blades' playing coach, watching from behind the glass with a coffee and a notebook.
ladder.travel: Carpool to Harlow Falls, the first real away rink.
ladder.headline: Harlow Falls Herald: 'Millbrook Newcomer Heads to A Division, Grudges Await'

ladder.scout: Hap Doyle's nephew, in a Millmen jacket, who never takes notes and never needs to. A letter arrives on Kessler letterhead.
ladder.travel: The rented yellow school bus, which has a Senior team on it and smells like it.
ladder.headline: Kessler Courier: 'Beer Leaguer Invited to Millmen Camp; Doyle: "We'll See"'

ladder.scout: A man in an ILHL windbreaker with a clipboard and a stopwatch, who drives four hours to see one shift.
ladder.travel: A coach bus nicknamed the Gas Can Express. You get gas money and a meal per diem of $11.
ladder.headline: Port Ainsley Lakesider: 'Senior Standout Signs Semi-Pro Deal (Gas Money Included)'

ladder.scout: A CHA scout with a laminated lanyard and a GNHL parent club logo on his tablet. In the valley it might be Ronnie Haverstock himself, who hands you the Dukes' phone number after the Thursday old-timers' game.
ladder.travel: Charter coach with wifi that never works, hotel rooms with a roommate.
ladder.headline: Duncannon Daily Ledger, front of sports: 'From Late Ice to the Dukes: Valley's Own Gets the Call'

ladder.scout: The phone call. In Duncannon it is the red rotary phone on Lorne Pettigrew's desk, ringing for Kingsport at 6:40 am.
ladder.travel: A plane. Your first one with a team logo on the tail.
ladder.headline: Every paper in the valley, front page: 'One of Ours in the Show'

promotion.relegation: Getting cut at a tryout or released is handled kindly by the world: your old team welcomes you back, the Clarion runs 'Back Where He Belongs', and the postgame pitcher is on the house.
